column1: # Provenance is a COLUMN, one value per row, in the sixth field:
#   claim      -- the intent was written by reading the CITING SENTENCE first: the
#                 sentence fixes the work, and the locator was then found for that
#                 work.  For these rows the support test is a genuine check.
#   backfilled -- the intent is the title of the record the LOCATOR returned, so for
#                 these rows the support test asserts only that the locator agrees
#                 with itself.  This is the blind spot the round-3 review found live
#                 in `pbft`, and it is now bounded per row rather than declared as a
# The rule by which a row got its mark: `claim` iff the locator was chosen by reading
# the sentence -- the rows corrected in the round-1 repair (derivable: their (method,
# value) differs from the batch at commit 1ada0e2) plus the two corrected this round.
# The number is COUNTED from this column by verify_refs.py, not declared here: the
# previous header carried a bare count (20) that the tree could not derive, so a
# reviewer could not run the check it described.  The number of corrected locators the
# tree can derive is 16; the two sets are not the same set, and only the column is
# What the column does and does not do: the MARK is still a declaration by the
# author -- no rule can recover, from a row, who wrote what when. What changes is
# that the blind spot is now per ROW and spot-checkable: a reviewer can take any row
# marked `claim`, read its citing sentence, and decide whether that record is the
# work the sentence needs. Before this column the same review question could not be
# run at all, because the split was one number in a header the rows could not confirm.
# (Columns: key, method, value, declared intent, optional author, provenance,
# Batch 1 of the bibliography, clusters A-E. Format: key <TAB> doi|arxiv|title <TAB> value
# Every line is verified before it is cited; an unverified line is dropped, not softened.
# Batch 2 of the bibliography, clusters F-J plus the estimation-theory block.
# Column 7 (`anchor`) records how each row's anchoring was established, one value
# per row: `screen` -- the citing clause in the manuscript names the record by a
# token of its title that exactly ONE title in this corpus carries, or by one of its
# authors' surnames; `read` -- the screen cannot decide (no unique title token and no
# surname), so the clause was READ against the record by the author -- identity and
# all: the returned year, venue and authors against the entry's own line.
# The screen detects UNEARNED SILENCE, not substitution: a substitute that shares the
# record's own unique token passes it, and the selftest pins that clause as a blind
# spot. A `screen` mark is therefore a statement about the clause's vocabulary, not a
# certification of identity; the identity reads are what cover the rest.
# Sixteen rows were `screen` under the older rule (a token shared by up to two titles
# was accepted, which is how `byzantine` certified a clause about another work) and
# are `read` here: each was read against its record and every one is correctly
# anchored, so the rule changed what the instrument may assert, not any verdict.
# verify_refs.py recomputes the screen and FAILS if a mark disagrees with it or if a
# flagged row is left unread, so the column cannot drift away from the instrument.
# `detectiontheory` (a title search with no matching record) was dropped here: it is
# cited by no sentence, and an unverifiable citation must not be shipped.
